messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Telugu, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Telugu line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
106 ఆ వినయపూర్ణ ఇటలీకి రక్షణ అవుతుంది 107 ఆ రక్షణ కోసం కన్యా కామిల్లా మరణించింది, 108 యూరియాలో, టర్నో, నిసో గాయపడినవారు.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (Eng.) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|--------------------------|--------| | Di | “of” (genitive) | ఇటలీకి | “to/for Italy” (case suffix) | OK | | quella | demonstrative “that” | ఆ | “that” | OK | | umile | “humble” | వినయపూర్ణ | “humble” | OK | | Italia | proper noun “Italy” | ఇటలీ | “Italy” | OK | | fia | future copula “shall be” | ఉంటుంది | “will be” | OK | | salute | “salvation” | రక్షణ | “salvation / rescue” | OK | | per | causal/prepositional “for” | కోసం | “for / because of” | OK | | cui | relative pronoun “which/that” | ఆ | “that” | OK | | morì | simple past “died” | మరణించింది | “died” | OK | | la | definite article “the” | — (omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | vergine | “virgin” (title) | కన్యా | “virgin” | OK | | Cammilla | proper name “Camilla” | కామిల్లా | “Camilla” | OK | | Eurialo | proper name “Eurialo” | యూరియాలో | “Eurialo‑LOC” (adds locative suffix) | WRONG | | e (1st) | coordinating conjunction “and” | — (comma used) | — | UNNECESSARY | | Turno | proper name “Turnus” | టర్నో | “Turnus” | OK | | e (2nd) | coordinating conjunction “and” | — (comma used) | — | UNNECESSARY | | Niso | proper name “Nisus” | నిసో | “Nisus” | OK | | di | preposition “of” (introducing state) | — (omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | ferute | “wounded” (state) | గాయపడినవారు | “the wounded (people)” | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **WRONG**: **Eurialo → యూరియాలో** – the Telugu suffix *‑లో* makes the name locative (“in Eurialo”), which is not present in the source. - **UNNECESSARY**: - **la** (definite article) – Telugu does not use articles. - **e** (both occurrences) – conjunction omitted; commas serve the coordination. - **di** (preposition) – the state “wounded” is expressed directly by the participial adjective, so the preposition is not needed.
All other mappings are **OK**.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Telugu script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 106: - Original: ఆ వినయపూర్ణ ఇటలీకి రక్షణ అవుతుంది - Issue: none - Corrected: ఆ వినయపూర్ణ ఇటలీకి రక్షణ అవుతుంది
- Line 107: - Original: ఆ రక్షణ కోసం కన్యా కామిల్లా మరణించింది, - Issue: none - Corrected: ఆ రక్షణ కోసం కన్యా కామిల్లా మరణించింది,
- Line 108: - Original: యూరియాలో, టర్నో, నిసో గాయపడినవారు. - Issue: none - Corrected: యూరియాలో, టర్నో, నిసో గాయపడినవారు.
